# California Earned Income Tax Credit - Key Provisions

## Subdivision (a)(2)
"The amount of the credit determined under Section 32 of the Internal Revenue Code...shall be multiplied by the earned income tax credit adjustment factor."

## Refundable Credit
"If the amount allowable as a credit under this section exceeds the tax liability...the balance, if any, shall be paid from the Tax Relief and Refund Account and refunded to the taxpayer."

## Subdivision (c)(2) - Age Modification
For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2018, the IRC 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II) reference is modified by "deleting '25 but not attained age 65' and inserting in lieu thereof the following: '18.'"

## Subdivision (o) - Full Text

**Paragraph (1):** For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2019, if computed credit amounts fall below specified thresholds ($200 for no qualifying children; $505 for one or more), modified credit and phaseout percentages apply based on number of qualifying children.

**Paragraph (2):** Corresponding earned income and phaseout amounts are adjusted for the same threshold conditions.

**Paragraph (3):** Through the year minimum wage reaches $15/hour, amounts recompute annually per income tax bracket rules, with phaseout percentages recalculated so credit equals zero at $30,000 earned income.

**Paragraph (4):** After minimum wage reaches $15/hour, annual recomputation continues using prior-year phaseout percentages.

# 26 U.S. Code § 32 - Key Provisions

## Section 32(a)(2) - Limitation

The credit limit is determined as the excess of:

**(A)** "the credit percentage of the earned income amount" over

**(B)** "the phaseout percentage of so much of the adjusted gross income (or, if greater, the earned income) of the taxpayer for the taxable year as exceeds the phaseout amount."

This provision uses whichever is greater between adjusted gross income and earned income when calculating the phaseout reduction.

## Section 32(c)(2)(A)(i) - Earned Income Definition

Earned income encompasses "wages, salaries, tips, and other employee compensation, but only if such amounts are includible in gross income for the taxable year."

This requirement ensures only amounts actually included in the taxpayer's reported gross income qualify toward the earned income credit calculation.
